meaning.evidence: All facts kept: three F-5s, the Jets vs Browns game, the 10 to 1 Experience Zone, Artemis dome, inflatable SLS, MAX POWER on Nov. 7 and 8, the 250th anniversary. Additions are colour: "Now here's one for the gridiron fans.", "roaring over to kick off".

sense.evidence: Terms fit their context: "at the stick of one of three F-5 fighter jets", "having a yarn with the fans", "the uni mob" for academia, "driverless vehicles" for autonomous vehicles, "down the track" for the future.

authenticity.evidence: Natural Australian: "a whopping great inflatable", "have a crack at the hands-on games", "a multi-day do", "down the track". One US form: "public sector folks".

register.evidence: Right about level 4: most sentences retold in Aussie ("The Inspiration Tour's pulling up all over the country", "The whole show wraps up") without tipping into a pub yarn. No swearing, within vulgarity 1.

tone.evidence: Keeps the upbeat promotional tone of the release: "it's a multi-day do that's good for the whole family, showing off the next-gen aircraft".

flow.evidence: Reads well; the last sentence is long ("Put on to honour America's historic 250th anniversary, it's a multi-day do that's good for the whole family, showing off").

variety.evidence: Varied throughout: "at the stick", "roaring over", "having a yarn", "pop under", "have a crack", "snap a few pics", "uni mob", "hook the agency up", "wraps up", "know-how".

essence.evidence: Unmistakably the NASA flyover notice, same order and content: "MAX POWER, a public expo of American air and space know-how".

problems.why: "folks" is American; an Australian would say people or mob.

A.summary: Lively, natural and accurate, at the right level-4 weight; the best of the three.

meaning.evidence: All facts kept in the original order: "to get the New York Jets vs. Cleveland Browns game underway", "from 10 a.m. to 1 p.m. EDT", "on Saturday, Nov. 7, and Sunday, Nov. 8". Nothing invented.

authenticity.evidence: Natural throughout: "the academic, industry and public sector mob", "have a go at the hands-on games", "the multi-day, family-friendly do". Nothing American left in.

register.evidence: A shade lighter than level 4: the first sentence is nearly the original, and terms like "next-generation aircraft, spacecraft, autonomous vehicles and technologies" are kept as written. No swearing.

tone.evidence: Keeps the promotional tone: "so the agency can link up with the people, technologies and organisations that keep America out in front in space."

flow.evidence: Reads smoothly, like it was written that way: "With stops right round the country, NASA’s Inspiration Tour gets the academic, industry and public sector mob together".

variety.evidence: Varied: "at the controls", "having a yarn", "rock up", "have a go", "snap a few pics", "mob", "show-and-tell", "down the track".

essence.evidence: Clearly the original release, retold: "The whole tour wraps up with MAX POWER".

B.summary: Smooth, faithful and natural, a touch lighter than level 4, with one belittling choice in "show-and-tell".
